The application is built, verified, and ready for your review.

**Open it at: http://maker:4000**

**What was done.** I built the app fresh in `implementation/` from the approved behaviours (not from the exploration prototypes), as a small web app: a Node backend (bookmarks, saved views, and settings persist to disk; it also fetches page details, saves offline copies, submits to the Internet Archive, and handles import/export) with a responsive browser interface.

**Verification — all passed:**
- **18 internal unit tests** covering the search query language, the bookmark-file import/export (including folders-becoming-tags), page-detail extraction, and the address rules.
- **A full browser walkthrough** of all 18 approved behaviours: saving, no-duplicates, editing, tags with suggestions, include/exclude tag filtering, everyday and advanced search, Markdown notes, read-tracking, archive vs. delete, bulk actions on whole result sets, sorting/paging/text-size with a saved default, saved views, and import/export.

**Two honesty notes about the trial environment:**
- Fetching a page's details, saving a self-contained copy, and the PDF-saving all work — I verified them against a local stand-in website (inlined CSS, images embedded, PDF stored). In normal use these reach the real site; in this sandbox the open internet isn't available, so a save of a real live URL falls back to keeping the link with a title from its address (exactly the "save anyway" behaviour we agreed), and a failed offline copy reports the failure and lets you retry — never losing the bookmark.
- Internet Archive preservation is implemented with its retry-on-failure handling; its success depends on the runtime being able to reach web.archive.org.

The deferred **by-website view** remains for a later round, and large-collection **performance** stays a separate quality concern, as agreed.

**Do you accept this software and agree to complete this cycle?** If you find anything that doesn't match a behaviour we approved, tell me and I'll correct it within this cycle; anything that changes or adds to what we approved I'll record for the next round.
